Key research papers on multi-agent orchestration, grouped by surveys, framework architectures, and evaluation benchmarks:

### Comprehensive Surveys and Taxonomies

*   [Large Language Model based Multi-Agents: A Survey of Progress and Challenges](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.01680) (Guo et al., 2024, arXiv)
    *   **Focus:** Core multi-agent coordination dimensions: agent profiling, communication mechanisms/topologies, simulation environments (problem-solving vs. world simulation), and capacity growth mechanisms.
*   [Beyond Self-Talk: A Communication-Centric Survey of LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.14321) (Yan et al., 2025, *Frontiers of Computer Science*)
    *   **Focus:** Communication-centric taxonomy covering message routing, topological structures, and collective interaction paradigms.
*   [A Survey of Agentic Reasoning for Large Language Models: Towards Recursively Self-Improving and Collective Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.12538) (Wei et al., 2026, *TMLR*)
    *   **Focus:** Three-dimensional framing spanning foundational reasoning, environment interaction dynamics, and recursive self-improving collective multi-agent architectures.

---

### Foundational Orchestration Frameworks and Execution Protocols

*   [AutoGen: Enabling Next-Gen LLM Applications via Multi-Agent Conversation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.08155) (Wu et al., 2023, Technical Report)
    *   **Mechanism:** Conversational topology programming. Models orchestration as two-agent chat, sequential chat, and dynamic group chat managed by a `GroupChatManager` with tool use and human-in-the-loop controls.
*   [MetaGPT: Meta Programming for A Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework](https://openreview.net/forum?id=VtmBAGCN7o) (Hong et al., 2023/2024, ICLR 2024)
    *   **Mechanism:** Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) assembly-line orchestration. Implements publish-subscribe shared message pools, role-specific observation filters, and structured intermediate outputs (PRDs, system designs).
*   [ChatDev: Communicative Agents for Software Development](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.07924) (Qian et al., 2023, ACL 2024)
    *   **Mechanism:** Waterfall software development lifecycle (SDLC) phase coordination. Deconstructs tasks into sequential phases (design, code, test, document) using paired conversational sub-dialogues with reflection loops.
*   [AgentVerse: Facilitating Multi-Agent Collaboration and Exploring Emergent Behaviors in Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.10848) (Chen et al., 2023/2024, ICLR 2024)
    *   **Mechanism:** Dynamic multi-stage protocol. Coordinates tasks through dynamic expert recruitment, collaborative decision-making, action execution, and evaluation/refinement loops.
*   [VillagerAgent: A Graph-Based Multi-Agent Framework for Coordinating Complex Task Dependencies in Minecraft](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.05720) (Dong et al., 2024, ACL 2024)
    *   **Mechanism:** Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) dependency orchestration. Schedules agent execution by mapping prerequisite dependencies and sub-goals onto dynamic causal graphs.

---

### Benchmarks and Evaluation Metrics

*   [OrchBench: Evaluating Multi-Agent Orchestration Plans in Isolation via Deterministic Simulation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25656) (Ren et al., 2026, arXiv)
    *   **Metrics:** Evaluates orchestration plans using DAG simulation against task completion quality, makespan (latency), token cost overhead, and coordination failures across context budgets.
*   [AgentWebBench: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Coordination in Agentic Web](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.10938) (Zhong et al., 2026, arXiv)
    *   **Metrics:** Benchmarks coordination efficiency, communication overhead, and information exchange between decentralized web-agent providers versus centralized retrieval.
*   [The price of decentralization in managing engineering systems through multi-agent reinforcement learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.11884) (Bhustali et al., 2026, arXiv)
    *   **Metrics:** Quantifies performance degradation and coordination overhead incurred when shifting from centralized controllers to decentralized multi-agent policies.
*   [CalBench: Evaluating Coordination-Privacy Trade-offs in Multi-Agent LLMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.09823) (Zou et al., 2026, arXiv)
    *   **Metrics:** Measures negotiation overhead, communication failure modes, and privacy trade-offs in delegate agent-to-agent negotiations.

---

### Missing Information and Limitations

*   Full-text PDF data extraction was not performed; granular sub-taxonomies (e.g., exact mathematical formulations of centralized vs. decentralized routing graphs) and empirical numerical tables for `AgentWebBench` and `The price of decentralization` were not extracted beyond their abstracts and metadata.
*   External literature databases (Google Scholar, Papers with Code) were not reached due to browser step limits.

### Findings
- [AutoGen: Enabling Next-Gen LLM Applications via Multi-Agent Conversation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.08155) | **Authors:** Qingyun Wu, Gagan Bansal, Jieyu Zhang, Yiran Wu, Beibin Li, Erkang Zhu, Li Jiang, Xiaoyun Zhang, Chi Wang | **Year:** 2023 | **Venue:** arXiv / Technical Report | **Citations:** 2,873+ | **Orchestration Mechanism:** Multi-agent conversation programming. Models multi-agent workflows as conversational topologies (two-agent chat, sequential chat, and dynamic group chat managed by a GroupChatManager). Agents communicate through structured and unstructured message-passing and can execute tool code and integrate human-in-the-loop feedback | **Evidence:** Paper defines AutoGen as enabling next-generation LLM applications via multi-agent conversation, unifying complex execution workflows through automated agent chats | **Relevance:** Seminal multi-agent conversational orchestration platform widely adopted across industry and research.

- [MetaGPT: Meta Programming for A Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework](https://openreview.net/forum?id=VtmBAGCN7o) | **Authors:** Sirui Hong, Mingchen Zhuge, Jonathan Chen, Xiawu Zheng, Cheng Hao, Ceyao Zhang, Jinlin Wang, Zili Wang, Steven Ka Shing Yau, Zijuan Lin, Liyang Zhou, Chenglin Wu, Jürgen Schmidhuber | **Year:** 2023 / 2024 | **Venue:** ICLR 2024 | **Citations:** 2,595+ | **Orchestration Mechanism:** Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) workflow orchestration and assembly-line paradigm. Encodes human procedural SOPs into prompt sequences, role definitions, and structured output formats (PRD, System Design, Data API). Agents coordinate asynchronously via a shared message pool (publish-subscribe pattern) and role-specific observation filters | **Evidence:** Page states MetaGPT incorporates human workflows into multi-agent collaboration via an assembly line paradigm, assigning specialized roles with intermediate verification to reduce error cascades | **Relevance:** Introduces foundational SOP-driven and assembly-line coordination for LLM multi-agent systems.

- [ChatDev: Communicative Agents for Software Development](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.07924) | **Authors:** Cheng Qian, Wei Liu, Hongzhi Gao, Dang Yufan, Yujia Qin, Cheng Yang, Zhiyuan Liu, Maosong Sun | **Year:** 2023 | **Venue:** ACL 2024 | **Citations:** 1,309+ | **Orchestration Mechanism:** Waterfall software development lifecycle (SDLC) multi-phase coordination. Decomposes tasks into sequential phases (Designing, Coding, Testing, Documenting), executing each phase via paired multi-agent communicative conversations (e.g., CEO-CPO, CTO-Programmer) with mutual multi-turn verification and reflection loops | **Evidence:** ACL publication demonstrates chat-powered software development where specialized role-playing agents communicate under guided dialogue protocols to solve tasks autonomously | **Relevance:** Seminal framework for phase-based sequential dialogic orchestration and agent role-play.

- [AgentVerse: Facilitating Multi-Agent Collaboration and Exploring Emergent Behaviors in Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.10848) | **Authors:** Weize Chen, Yusheng Su, Jingwei Zuo, Cheng Yang, Chenfei Yuan, Chi-Min Chan, Heyang Yu, Yujia Qin, Yaxi Lu, Shukang Yin, Shen Zhi, Junjie Wang, Dahai Li, Zhiyuan Liu, Maosong Sun, Jie Zhou | **Year:** 2023 / 2024 | **Venue:** ICLR 2024 | **Citations:** 815+ | **Orchestration Mechanism:** Dynamic multi-stage orchestration protocol. Organizes agent interaction through four distinct coordination stages: Expert Recruitment (dynamic role assignment), Collaborative Decision-Making (planning and consensus), Action Execution, and Evaluation/Refinement (feedback and adjustment) | **Evidence:** ICLR paper confirms dynamic multi-agent framework adjusting group composition as a greater-than-the-sum-of-its-parts system with dynamic roles and feedback loops | **Relevance:** Foundational work introducing dynamic agent recruitment, runtime adaptation, and multi-stage consensus protocols.

- [VillagerAgent: A Graph-Based Multi-Agent Framework for Coordinating Complex Task Dependencies in Minecraft](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.05720) | **Authors:** Yu-Bo Dong, Xukun Zhu, Zheng Pan, Linchao Zhu, Yi Yang | **Year:** 2024 | **Venue:** ACL 2024 | **Citations:** 58 | **Orchestration Mechanism:** Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) task-dependency orchestration. Builds dynamic task graphs where nodes represent sub-goals and directed edges encode causal execution prerequisites, coordinating agent scheduling and dependency resolution | **Evidence:** ACL publication introduces a DAG multi-agent framework to resolve complex inter-agent dependencies and enhance collaborative workflow efficiency in dynamic simulation environments | **Relevance:** Key representative paper for explicit graph-based topological orchestration in multi-agent LLM systems.

### Coverage
- Searched Semantic Scholar via direct queries:
  - `"multi-agent" orchestration framework LLM` (~7,920 results returned; reviewed page 1)
  - `MetaGPT OR AutoGen OR ChatDev OR AgentVerse` (9 citation-ranked papers reviewed)

  - `"AutoGen: Enabling Next-Gen LLM Applications via Multi-Agent Conversation"` (2 entries verified)
  - `"Communicative Agents for Software Development" OR "AgentVerse"` (16 results reviewed)
- Reviewed approximately 40 result entries total across Semantic Scholar queries to isolate seminal framework papers introducing distinct orchestration paradigms (conversation-based, SOP-based, phase-based, dynamic recruitment, and DAG-based).

### Limitations

### Findings
- [OrchBench: Evaluating Multi-Agent Orchestration Plans in Isolation via Deterministic Simulation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25656) | **Authors:** Zhenzhen Ren, Jiyan He, Xinpeng Zhang, Zhenxing Qian, Ke Han, Shuxin Zheng, GuoBiao Li, Xiaoqing Zhang | **Year:** 2026 | **Venue:** arXiv preprint (`cs.AI`, arXiv:2607.25656) | **Benchmark focus & metrics:** Benchmark for multi-agent orchestration plans using directed acyclic graph (DAG) simulation; evaluates task completion quality, makespan (latency/efficiency), token cost overhead, and coordination failures across varying agent budgets and context limits | **Evidence:** Paper demonstrates simulated orchestration scores correlate with Claude Code execution at Pearson $r=0.816$ while using $1.3\%$ of tokens and $10.3\%$ of wall-clock time; findings show preserving task-critical information outweighs scaling agent counts, and parallelism gains diminish as coordination failures accumulate | **Relevance:** Directly establishes quantitative metrics (result quality, makespan, token overhead) and coordination failure trade-offs for multi-agent orchestration.

- [AgentWebBench: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Coordination in Agentic Web](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.10938) | **Authors:** Shanshan Zhong, Kate Shen, Chenyan Xiong | **Year:** 2026 | **Venue:** arXiv preprint (`cs.MA`, arXiv:2604.10938) | **Benchmark focus & metrics:** Benchmarking multi-agent coordination across decentralized agentic web environments versus centralized retrieval paradigms, focusing on coordination efficiency and cross-agent communication | **Evidence:** Investigates the transition from centralized information retrieval to decentralized coordination where content-provider agents serve data through interfaces | **Relevance:** Addresses decentralized vs. centralized coordination performance and communication efficiency across autonomous agents.

- [The price of decentralization in managing engineering systems through multi-agent reinforcement learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.11884) | **Authors:** Prateek Bhustali, Pablo G. Morato, Konstantinos G. Papakonstantinou, Charalampos P. Andriotis | **Year:** 2026 | **Venue:** arXiv preprint (`cs.MA`, arXiv:2603.11884) | **Benchmark focus & metrics:** Quantitative comparison and evaluation of the "price of decentralization" in multi-agent orchestration against centralized baselines; evaluates scalability, coordination efficiency, and performance trade-offs | **Evidence:** Directly benchmarks multi-component coordination policies to quantify performance loss and overhead incurred by shifting from centralized controllers to decentralized multi-agent architectures | **Relevance:** Provides direct quantitative analysis of centralized versus decentralized orchestration efficiency.
